slides.title: Your icons are making your firm look [assembled].
slides.lede: Iconography works when it makes a complex firm easier to understand without making it feel simpler or less credible.

slides.title: Not every icon should [do the same work]

cards.label: Functional icons
cards.text: Help people act: download, filter, save, warning. Comprehension comes first.

cards.label: Expressive icons
cards.text: Carry themes and character. They frame ideas rather than control anything.

slides.title: Consistency comes from [repeatable rules], not a mood board
slides.note: New icons should feel **built from the same grammar**, not merely drawn in a similar style.

slides.title: Start with the [smallest real use]
slides.text: At 16 pixels, a scale, a handshake, a bar chart and a shield can become indistinguishable. Keep size-specific variants when the meaning would otherwise collapse.

slides.quote: If choosing the wrong interpretation would lead to the wrong action, include text.
slides.text: A document icon beside a button may be unclear. Download engagement terms is not.

items.title: Name and meaning
items.text: What it stands for, in words.

items.title: Permitted contexts
items.text: Where it may appear, and at what sizes.

items.title: Accessibility label
items.text: Or the text it must sit beside.

slides.title: Give every icon a job, a language and a place.
slides.lede: Brand iconography that makes complex firms easier to understand. Read the full guide via the link in our bio.
